title: PGFuzz, NDSS 2021
locator: Abstract; Sec. I (fail-safe MTL example and distance metrics); Sec. III threat model (self-sabotaging inputs out of scope); Table II policy list incl. A.RC.FS1/FS2, A.GPS.FS1, PX.GPS.FS1/FS2, A.ALIVE; Sec. VI implementation (Pymavlink, three autopilots); Table VII bug summary
evidence_grade: B for the inspected sections (peer-reviewed venue, method and policy table read directly)
finding: PGFuzz fuzzes commands, parameters and environment against 56 MTL policies per autopilot, with a distance metric to a policy violation. locator: README.md (Cases 1-2: parachute; PX4 GPS fail-safe COM_POS_FS_DELAY; Sec. 6 bitcode notes); ArduPilot/fuzzing.py L145-200 (Current_policy selector, check_liveness: no HEARTBEAT for 5 s => 'program crashed' => reboot) and policy blocks A.CHUTE, A.RTL1-4, A.FLIP1-4, A.ALT_HOLD1-2, A.CIRCLE1-3/7, A.LAND1-2, A.AUTO1, A.GPS.FS1-2 (L1850-1930), A.RC.FS1-2 (L1931-1990: FS_THR_VALUE vs RC channel 3, RC_failsafe flag), A.SPORT1, A.GUIDED1, A.LOITER1, A.DRIFT1, A.BRAKE1; PX4/fuzzing.py L126-165 and blocks PX.CHUTE, PX.RTL1, PX.ALTITUDE1, PX.HOLD1-2, PX.POSITION1, PX.TAKEOFF1-2, PX.LAND1, PX.GPS.FS1-3 (L1738-1830: GPS_loss, gps_failsafe flag, COM_POS_FS_DELAY, RC channels, ALTCTL mode); PX4/check_policy.py (FLIP altitude and RTL-altitude policies); ArduPilot/update_distance.py (per-policy altitude/roll/pitch/heading error distance)
evidence_grade: C (released research code, read not run; policy set in code is narrower than the paper's Table II)
finding: Released code holds separate ArduPilot/ and PX4/ trees with separate hard-coded policy lists and MAVLink handlers; no shared policy vocabulary or mapping between the two. RC and GPS fail-safe policies from U2 Table II are implemented (A.RC.FS1-2, A.GPS.FS1-2, PX.GPS.FS1-3) as state predicates over telemetry and parameters (FS_THR_VALUE vs RC throttle, GPS status, COM_POS_FS_DELAY, mode) that score distance to a policy violation; the fuzzer drives them by mutating parameters, commands and simulated environment, not by cutting a GCS/offboard link or a setpoint stream. No A.ALIVE identifier exists in the released Python; heartbeat absence (5 s) is a crash oracle that reboots the simulator. Distance guidance is per-policy state error, matching U2's policy-violation distance. Nothing about reconnection or command return; no cross-autopilot policy equivalence.

title: ADGFuzz: Assignment Dependency-Guided Fuzzing for Robotic Vehicles, NDSS 2026
locator: Abstract; Sec. I; Sec. III-C threat model (GCS spoofing / link hijacking named as attacker tactics, out of the bug class studied); Sec. IV (MIS entropy scheduling; oracles: crash on ground, route deviation over a 7 s window, software crash = no heartbeat for 2 s); Sec. evidence_grade: B for the inspected sections (peer-reviewed venue, method, setup and bug table read directly)
finding: Fuzzes ArduPilot-only (Copter, Plane, Rover in SITL) for assignment-statement bugs using a static assignment dependency graph and entropy-scheduled matched input sets. Heartbeat absence is used as a crash ORACLE (2 s), never injected as a fault; loss of GCS communication caused by SYSID_THISMAV is classified as a false positive and excluded. One reported bug (Rover, bug 40) is a failsafe-behaviour defect (fence violation without RTL), found as a bug instance, not as a comparison of recovery behaviour across configurations. No PX4 evaluation, no reconnection or command-return phase, no coverage measure of a recovery trajectory (coverage in the paper means code/MIS coverage).

evidence_grade: B for the inspected sections (peer-reviewed venue, author-posted full text read directly)
finding: Automated program repair for logic bugs in ArduPilot, PX4 and Paparazzi, driven by per-autopilot PPL formulas. This is the nearest neighbour in FORM to a per-autopilot recovery contract, but no formula is defined as equivalent across autopilots or pinned configurations, no comparison of realised behaviour is made, and the ArduPilot GCS-failsafe function appears only as a code-mapping location. Link loss and setpoint loss are not injected; what happens when inputs return is not a formula; no trajectory coverage measure.
